text.p: Infrastructure Trust said on Monday it had requested a trading halt to be applied to its shares pending an announcement on the successful bidder for the Loy Yang A power station in Victoria.
Infrastructure units closed on Friday three cents lower at A$1.27.
The sale of the 2,000 megawatt station and associated coal mine was likely to fetch around A$4.5 billion for the Victorian state government, a source told Reuters last week.
This compares with a value of around A$5 billion quoted in recent newspaper reports.

Final bids for Loy Yang A, the biggest and most modern power station to be privatised by the Victoria government, closed last Thursday. The announcement of the winning bid is expected to be announced this week.
